items.title: Data Alpha Portfolio
items.text:
Documentation for developing, customizing, and contributing to the Data Alpha Portfolio.

Data Alpha is a statically generated portfolio for writing about data, AI, and finance. It uses Astro 4, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MDX, and Astro Content Collections.

items.title: Component Reference
items.text: Reference for UI components used in the Data Alpha Portfolio project.

items.title: Available Components
items.text: Components live in src/components/. Astro components render the static page structure, while React components provide reusable or interactive UI.

items.title: Button
items.text:
Accepts standard React button attributes plus:

  • variant: primary, secondary, or outline; defaults to primary
  • size: sm, md, or lg; defaults to md

items.title: Card
items.text: Accepts standard React div attributes plus variant: default, elevated, or outlined. The default is default.

items.title: Content Components
items.text:
• BlogPreview renders a collection of blog summaries.
  • ProjectGrid renders project summaries, technology tags, and optional demo/source links.
  • TagList accepts a tags: string[] prop and renders nothing for an empty list.
  • ContactForm provides client-side validation and currently simulates submission; it is not connected to a form service.

items.title: Astro Components
items.text:
• Layout, Header, and Footer provide shared page structure.
  • SEO and SchemaOrg generate metadata and structured data.
  • AboutSection, ExperienceSection, and SkillsSection render portfolio sections.
  • BlogPost renders blog article content.

Import components from src/components/ using their named or default export as defined in each file.

items.title: Code Style
items.text: Coding conventions and style guidelines for the Data Alpha Portfolio project.

items.title: JavaScript/TypeScript
items.text:
• Use 2-space indentation (no tabs)
  • Prefer const and let over var
  • Use template literals for string interpolation
  • Preserve the repository's semicolon and single-quote style
  • Add explicit types where they improve public component contracts
  • Use PascalCase for components and types, camelCase for variables and functions

items.title: Markdown/MDX
items.text:
• Use lowercase file names with hyphens as separators
  • Keep lines under 100 characters when possible
  • Use fenced code blocks with language specifiers
  • Include proper frontmatter for content collections
  • Write in clear, concise language

items.title: CSS/Tailwind
items.text:
• Use utility-first approach with Tailwind CSS
  • Reserve custom CSS for complex animations or keyframes
  • Follow responsive design principles
  • Use semantic HTML elements where possible

items.title: Commit Messages
items.text:
Follow the Conventional Commits specification:

  • feat: for new features
  • fix: for bug fixes
  • docs: for documentation changes
  • style: for formatting changes
  • refactor: for code refactoring
  • test: for test-related changes
  • chore: for maintenance tasks

items.title: Code Review Process
items.text:
Run the checks that apply to your change:

npm run build
npx astro check
uv run zensical build

Update documentation when behavior or public interfaces change. Request review from maintainers, address feedback, and squash commits if requested.

items.title: Personal Website Implementation Plan
items.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Build a personal portfolio website with blog, projects showcase, and about page using Astro 4.0 + React, hosted on GitHub Pages.

Architecture: Static site generated with Astro using file-based routing, MDX for content, Tailwind CSS for styling, and TypeScript for type safety. Content organized in collections for blog posts and projects.

Tech Stack: Astro 4.0, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MDX, GitHub Pages

items.title: Global Constraints
items.text:
• Must generate pure static HTML/CSS/JS (no server-side rendering)
  • Content must be stored as MDX files in /src/content
  • Must deploy to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions
  • Must include blog, projects showcase, and about pages
  • Must include contact form (via third-party service)
  • Must be fully responsive and accessible
  • Must include SEO optimizations (meta tags, sitemap)
  • Must use TypeScript for all JavaScript/TSX files
  • Must use Tailwind CSS for styling
  • Must be compatible with Astro 4.0 stable release

import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content';

const blogCollection = defineCollection({
  type: 'content',
  schema: z.object({
    title: z.string(),
    description: z.string(),
    pubDate: z.date(),
    updatedDate: z.date().optional(),
    heroImage: z.string().optional(),
    tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
    draft: z.boolean().default(false)
  })
});

const projectsCollection = defineCollection({
  type: 'content',
  schema: z.object({
    title: z.string(),
    description: z.string(),
    pubDate: z.date(),
    updatedDate: z.date().optional(),
    heroImage: z.string().optional(),

    demoUrl: z.string().url().optional(),
    sourceUrl: z.string().url().optional(),

export const collections = {
  blog: blogCollection,

# Getting Started with Data Analysis

Welcome to your journey into data analysis! In this post, we'll cover the fundamental concepts and tools you need to begin analyzing data effectively.

## Why Data Analysis Matters

Data analysis helps us make informed decisions by uncovering patterns, trends, and insights hidden in raw data. Whether you're looking to improve business processes, conduct research, or simply understand the world better, data analysis skills are invaluable.

## Core Concepts

### 1. Data Collection
Gathering data from various sources including databases, APIs, surveys, and web scraping.

### 2. Data Cleaning
Preparing data for analysis by handling missing values, removing duplicates, and correcting inconsistencies.

### 3. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
Using statistical and visualization techniques to understand data distribution and relationships.

### 4. Statistical Analysis
Applying statistical methods to test hypotheses and draw conclusions.

### 5. Data Visualization
Creating charts, graphs, and dashboards to communicate findings effectively.

## Essential Tools

- **Python**: Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn
- **R**: Tidyverse, ggplot2
- **SQL**: For querying relational databases
- **Excel/Google Sheets**: For basic analysis and visualization
- **Tableau/Power BI**: For interactive dashboards

## Next Steps

Start with a small dataset and practice the complete workflow: collect, clean, analyze, and visualize. Try reproducing analyses from published papers or online tutorials to build your skills.

Remember, the key to becoming proficient in data analysis is consistent practice and curiosity about the data you're working with.

# Research Wiki

The Research Wiki is a collaborative knowledge base designed to help researchers organize, share, and build upon their findings. This project combines modern web technologies with intuitive design to create a powerful tool for academic and professional research.

## Features

- **Real-time Collaboration**: Multiple users can edit articles simultaneously
- **Version Control**: Track changes and revert to previous versions when needed
- **Advanced Search**: Full-text search with filters and tags
- **Reference Management**: Built-in citation tools supporting APA, MLA, and Chicago styles
- **Markdown Support**: Write and format content using familiar Markdown syntax
- **API Access**: Programmatic access to all wiki content via REST and GraphQL endpoints

## Technical Architecture

### Frontend
- React 18 with Hooks for state management
- Tailwind CSS for responsive design
- React Query for data fetching and caching
- Monaco Editor for rich text editing

### Backend
- Node.js with Express.js framework
- MongoDB for flexible document storage
- GraphQL API for efficient data queries
- WebSocket connections for real-time updates

## Key Learnings

Building this project taught me valuable lessons about:
1. **State Management**: Choosing the right solution for complex, real-time applications
2. **Database Design**: Modeling relationships in NoSQL databases for optimal query performance
3. **WebSocket Implementation**: Handling connection lifecycle and scaling considerations
4. **API Design**: Creating intuitive, versioned APIs that evolve with user needs
5. **DevOps**: Setting up CI/CD pipelines for automated testing and deployment

## Future Enhancements

- AI-powered content summarization and tagging
- Offline-first capabilities with service workers
- Enhanced collaboration features with conflict resolution
- Mobile app using React Native
- Advanced analytics dashboard for usage insights

## Get Started

Visit the live demo or check out the source code on GitHub to explore the Research Wiki further. Contributions are welcome!

  };

import { useState } from 'react';

interface FormValues {
  name: string;
  email: string;
  subject: string;
  message: string;
}

export const ContactForm = () => {
  const [formValues, setFormValues] = useState<FormValues>({
    name: '',
    email: '',
    subject: '',
    message: ''
  });

  const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false);
  const [submitStatus, setSubmitStatus] = useState<'idle' | 'success' | 'error'>('idle');
  const [submitMessage, setSubmitMessage] = useState('');

  const handleChange = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement>) => {
    const { name, value } = e.target;
    setFormValues(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: value }));
  };

  const handleSubmit = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    setIsSubmitting(true);
    setSubmitStatus('idle');

    try {
      // Simple validation
      if (!formValues.name || !formValues.email || !formValues.message) {
        throw new Error('Please fill in all required fields');
      }

      // Basic email validation
      const emailRegex = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;
      if (!emailRegex.test(formValues.email)) {
        throw new Error('Please enter a valid email address');
      }

      // In a real implementation, you would send this to a service like:
      // - Formspree
      // - Getform
      // - EmailJS
      // - Netlify Forms (if using Netlify)
      // For GitHub Pages, we'll use a third-party service

      // Simulate API call
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1500));

      setSubmitStatus('success');
      setSubmitMessage('Your message has been sent successfully! I\'ll get back to you soon.');
      setFormValues({
        name: '',
        email: '',
        subject: '',
        message: ''
      });
    } catch (error) {
      setSubmitStatus('error');
      setSubmitMessage(error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'An error occurred. Please try again.');
    } finally {
      setIsSubmitting(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} class="space-y-6">
      <div class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
        <div>
          <label htmlFor="name" class="block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-2">
            Name
          </label>
          <input
            id="name"
            name="name"
            type="text"
            required
            class="w-full px-4 py-3 border border-gray-300 rounded-md focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500 focus:border-indigo-500 sm:text-sm"
            value={formValues.name}
            onChange={handleChange}
          />
        </div>

        <div>
          <label htmlFor="email" class="block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-2">
            Email Address
          </label>
          <input
            id="email"
            name="email"
            type="email"
            required
            class="w-full px-4 py-3 border border-gray-300 rounded-md focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500 focus:border-indigo-500 sm:text-sm"
            value={formValues.email}
            onChange={handleChange}
          />
        </div>
      </div>

      <div>
        <label htmlFor="subject" class="block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-2">
          Subject
        </label>
        <input
          id="subject"
          name="subject"
          type="text"
          class="w-full px-4 py-3 border border-gray-300 rounded-md focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500 focus:border-indigo-500 sm:text-sm"
          value={formValues.subject}
          onChange={handleChange}
        />
      </div>

      <div>
        <label htmlFor="message" class="block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-2">
          Message
        </label>
        <textarea
          id="message"
          name="message"
          rows="5"
          required
          class="w-full px-4 py-3 border border-gray-300 rounded-md focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-500 focus:border-indigo-500 sm:text-sm"
          value={formValues.message}
          onChange={handleChange}
        />
      </div>

      {submitStatus !== 'idle' && (
        <div class={`mt-4 p-4 rounded-lg text-sm font-medium ${submitStatus === 'success' ? 'bg-green-50 text-green-800' : 'bg-red-50 text-red-800'} border ${submitStatus === 'success' ? 'border-green-200' : 'border-red-200'}`}>
          {submitMessage}
        </div>
      )}

      <button
        type="submit"
        disabled={isSubmitting}
        class="w-full px-6 py-3 bg-indigo-600 hover:bg-indigo-700 text-white font-medium rounded-md transition-colors hover:shadow-md disabled:opacity-50 disabled:pointer-events-none"
      >
        {isSubmitting ? 'Sending...' : 'Send Message'}
      </button>
    </form>
  );
};

# Personal Website

A personal portfolio website showcasing expertise in data, AI, and finance through blogging and project showcases.

## Features

- ✅ Blog with MDX support for rich content
- ✅ Project showcases with live demo/source links
- ✅ About page with bio, skills, and experience
- ✅ Contact form (via third-party service)
- ✅ Responsive design with Tailwind CSS
- ✅ SEO optimized (meta tags, schema, sitemap)
- ✅ Fast static site generation with Astro 4.0
- ✅ GitHub Pages deployment via GitHub Actions
- ✅ TypeScript for type safety
- ✅ Content collections for type-safe blog/projects

## Tech Stack

- **Framework**: [Astro 4.0](https://astro.build)
- **UI Library**: [React 18](https://reactjs.org)
- **Styling**: [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com)
- **Language**: [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org)
- **Content**: MDX with Astro Content Collections
- **Hosting**: GitHub Pages
- **Deployment**: GitHub Actions

## Local Development

1. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

2. Start development server:
   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```

3. Build for production:
   ```bash
   npm run build
   ```

4. Preview production build:
   ```bash
   npm run preview
   ```

## Deployment

# Authoring Content

This file provides guidance for creating content in the documentation.

## Content Guidelines

This file provides guidance for working with content in the `/docs/` directory.

## Content Exploration

Use standard text editor features or command-line tools when exploring content, frontmatter patterns, tags, internal links, or Markdown usage.

Examples:

- Use `grep` to find specific patterns
- Use your editor's search functionality to navigate content

## Content Structure

Content follows standard Markdown conventions:

- **Documentation Files**: Markdown files in `/docs/` and subdirectories
- **Sections**: Organized by topic in subdirectories

## Frontmatter Standards

Unlike the main project which uses YAML frontmatter for Astro Content Collections, this documentation uses plain Markdown without frontmatter for simplicity. If frontmatter is needed for specific features, it can be added as needed.

## Content Types

### Documentation Pages

- Located in `/docs/` subdirectories
- Use Markdown format
- Optional frontmatter for Zensical plugins or features

## Content Best Practices

1. Keep content focused: one topic per page.
2. Use descriptive filenames, such as `getting-started.md` or `api-reference.md`.
3. Optimize for readability with short paragraphs and clear headings.
4. Use consistent heading levels and formatting.
5. Use relative links for internal documentation references.
6. Keep indentation and formatting consistent.
7. Use standard Markdown syntax for emphasis, lists, code blocks, etc.

## Heading 2
### Heading 3

**Bold text**
*Italic text*
`Inline code`

## Documentation

This project includes contributor documentation powered by [Zensical](https://github.com/zensical/zensical) in the `/docs/` directory. The documentation is not automatically deployed but can be viewed locally for development and contribution purposes.

### Viewing Documentation Locally

To preview the documentation:

1. **Install Zensical** (choose one method):
   ```bash
   # Using pip and virtualenv
   python3 -m venv .venv
   source .venv/bin/activate
   pip install zensical

   # OR using uv (faster alternative)
   uv init
   uv add --dev zensical
   ```

2. **Start the preview server**:
   ```bash
   zensical serve
   ```

3. **View in browser**: Open <http://localhost:8000> to see the documentation

- **Getting Started** - Introduction to the project

items.title: Overview
items.text: This document details the design for modernizing three key components of the Data Alpha Portfolio website: the Header, Blog Preview, and Project Grid. The redesign follows Approach 1: Refined Minimalism with Data-Inspired Accents, chosen to enhance visual appeal and content presentation while maintaining a professional, approachable tone suitable for data/AI/finance professionals.

items.title: Goals Addressed
items.text:
• Visual Modernization: Elevate the visual design with contemporary refinements
  • Better Content Presentation: Improve scannability, hierarchy, and engagement with content
  • Audience Appropriateness: Maintain professional tone for data/AI/finance professionals and potential employers/clients

items.title: Design Principles Applied
items.text:
1. Refined Minimalism: Clean aesthetics with thoughtful enhancements rather than dramatic changes
  2. Data Sensitivity: Subtle use of accent colors and patterns that resonate with technical audiences
  3. Hierarchy & Scannability: Clear visual hierarchy to guide user attention
  4. Micro-interactions: Subtle feedback mechanisms to enhance engagement
  5. Consistency: Unified design language across components
  6. Performance Conscious: Lightweight implementations suitable for static sites

items.title: Visual Updates
items.text:
• Enhanced Background: bg-white/90 backdrop-blur-sm for subtle depth
  • Increased Height: h-20 (vs previous h-16) for better vertical spacing
  • Inner Border Treatment: Additional border-b border-gray-100/25 on inner container for depth
  • Active State Indicators: Clear visual feedback via bottom border (border-b-2) and text color changes
  • Refined Typography: Increased brand name size to text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tighter
  • Data-Inspired Accents: Indigo/blue color scheme + small dot in logo representing data points
  • Logo Treatment: Split styling ("Data Alpha" in gray, "Portfolio" in indigo) for visual hierarchy

items.title: Context
items.text:
The repository currently lacks comprehensive, centralized documentation. As the project grows, onboarding new contributors and helping users find setup guides, API reference docs, and usage examples becomes difficult. Developers must dig through raw Markdown files across directories or search through closed issues to find answers.

Issue #2 requests setting up a modern, hosted documentation site using Zensical, with documentation site setup, content architecture, automated deployment, and search & navigation.

items.title: Goals
items.text:
• Set up Zensical locally to author documentation in Markdown.
  • Organize documentation into clear sections: Getting Started, User Guide, API Reference, Contributing.
  • Provide instructions in the README for rendering the documentation locally.
  • Do not deploy the documentation site automatically; keep it as a local reference only (per user request).
  • Leverage Zensical's built-in search and navigation for a good developer experience.

items.title: Approach
items.text: We will add a /docs directory at the repository root containing the Zensical documentation source. The site will not be integrated into the existing Astro site nor deployed via GitHub Actions. Instead, we will update the README to explain how to install Zensical and preview the documentation locally.

items.title: Why Separate Docs Site?
items.text:
• Keeps documentation authoring simple with Zensical's conventions.
  • Avoids coupling documentation build with the main site's Astro build process.
  • Allows documentation to be worked on independently.

items.title: Why Not Deploy?
items.text: Per user feedback during design, the documentation will be set up locally only, with instructions in the README for anyone who wants to run it. This reduces complexity and avoids potential conflicts with the existing GitHub Pages deployment.

items.text:
• docs/content-guidelines.md will be moved to docs/user-guide/authoring.md and adapted to include Zensical‑specific authoring tips (though Zensical uses plain Markdown, we can note how to structure content, use headers, etc.).
  • The README will retain the project overview and gain a new “Documentation” section pointing to the local docs setup.

items.title: Implementation Steps
items.text:
1. Install Zensical locally (documented in README):
  2. Using pip: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install zensical
  3. Or using uv: uv init && uv add --dev zensical && uv run zensical
  4. Create the directory structure as shown above under /docs.
  5. Create placeholder Markdown files with minimal content (title, brief description, TODO comments) to ensure the site builds.
  6. Migrate docs/content-guidelines.md to docs/user-guide/authoring.md.
  7. Optionally add a basic zensical.toml at the repo root to configure site name, theme, etc. (not required for basic usage).
  8. Update README.md:
  9. Add a “Documentation” section after “Local Development” or “Deployment”.
  10. Include steps to install Zensical and run zensical serve from the repo root to preview docs at http://localhost:8000.
  11. Mention that the documentation is not deployed; it's for local reference only.
  12. Update .gitignore to ignore the generated site directory (default is docs/site/ if you build).

items.title: How to Run Locally (for README)
items.text:
After setting up the docs: 

# Optional: create a virtual environment
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install Zensical
pip install zensical

# Start the preview server
zensical serve
Then open http://localhost:8000 in your browser.

items.title: Acceptance Criteria
items.text:
• The /docs directory exists with the proposed structure.
  • Placeholder Markdown files are present and allow the Zensical server to start without errors.
  • The README includes clear instructions for installing Zensical and viewing the docs locally.
  • No changes are made to the existing GitHub Actions workflow (deploy.yml).
  • The documentation is not automatically deployed; it remains a local-only resource.

items.title: User Guide
items.text: Learn how to use, configure, and extend the Data Alpha Portfolio project.

items.title: Contents
items.text:
• Authoring Content - Writing Markdown and MDX content
  • Configuration - Project configuration files
  • Customization - Styling and theming options

items.title: Authoring Content
items.text: The portfolio content and the contributor documentation use separate authoring systems.

items.title: Portfolio Content
items.text:
Portfolio entries are MDX files in src/content/:

  • src/content/blog/ contains blog posts.
  • src/content/projects/ contains project pages.
  • src/content/about/index.mdx contains the About page content.

The collection schemas in src/content/config.ts validate frontmatter during the Astro build. Blog posts require title, description, and pubDate. Project entries require the same fields and may also provide demoUrl, sourceUrl, and techStack.

Example blog frontmatter:

---
title: "Analyzing a Dataset"
description: "A practical data-analysis walkthrough"
pubDate: 2026-07-31
tags: ["data-analysis", "tutorial"]
draft: false
---

Dates must be valid YAML dates. URLs in project frontmatter must be absolute URLs.

items.title: Documentation Content
items.text:
Documentation pages are Markdown files under docs/. Add user-facing pages to the nav section in the root mkdocs.yml so readers can discover them.

Use relative links between documentation pages:

[Configuration](./configuration.md)
[Contributing](../contributing/)

Put documentation images in docs/assets/ and reference them relative to the current source file:

![Architecture diagram](../assets/architecture.png)

items.title: Authoring Guidelines
items.text:
1. Keep content focused: one topic per page.
  2. Use descriptive lowercase filenames with hyphens.
  3. Optimize for readability with short paragraphs and clear headings.
  4. Use consistent heading levels and formatting.
  5. Use relative links and verify their targets.
  6. Add a language identifier to fenced code blocks.

items.title: Markdown Example
items.text:
# Heading 1
## Heading 2
### Heading 3

**Bold text**
*Italic text*
`Inline code`

```text
code block
```

- List item
- Another list item

[Link text](URL)

items.title: Configuration
items.text: The portfolio and documentation site have separate configuration files at the repository root.

items.title: Astro
items.text:
astro.config.mjs configures a static Astro site with React, Tailwind CSS, and MDX integrations. The deployed site uses:

site: 'https://deadhand777.github.io/data-alpha'
base: '/data-alpha/'
output: 'static'

Use import.meta.env.BASE_URL when building internal links in components so they work under the /data-alpha/ base path.

items.title: TypeScript
items.text: tsconfig.json extends Astro's strict preset and maps @/* to src/*.

items.title: Tailwind CSS
items.text: tailwind.config.cjs scans Astro, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and MDX files under src/. Theme colors are defined under theme.extend.colors; see Customization for the current palette.

items.title: Content Collections
items.text: src/content/config.ts defines the blog and projects schemas. Astro validates content against these schemas during npm run build.

items.title: Zensical
items.text:
mkdocs.yml defines the documentation site name and navigation. pyproject.toml pins Zensical as a development dependency, and uv.lock records the resolved Python environment.

This project does not currently require custom environment variables.

items.title: Styling
items.text:
The project uses Tailwind CSS utility classes. The main styling files are:

  • tailwind.config.cjs for content scanning and theme tokens
  • src/styles/global.css for Tailwind's base, component, and utility layers
  • Component files under src/components/ for page-level utility classes

items.title: Color Palette
items.text:
The Tailwind configuration defines semantic colors instead of a switchable theme:

Token Value Use bg-primary #0F172A Page background bg-surface #1E293B Cards and surfaces text-primary #F8FAFC Primary text text-secondary #E2E8F0 Secondary text accent-success #10B981 Positive actions accent-tech #3B82F6 Links and technical accents

Change these values in tailwind.config.cjs, then run npm run build to verify that every class is generated correctly.
